title: windowed-tenant-priority-throttler-with-consensus-reset-hotpatch
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Fix: Prevent double-throttling during regional failover by coordinating tenant throttle windows across regions and making circuit resets idempotent. Includes tests and dashboards to monitor per-tenant throttle rate.
body:
Context and motivation:
We observed multiple incidents where tenants experienced compounded throttling during cross-region failovers. The root cause was twofold: (1) the failover handoff path could temporarily apply a local tenant throttle in the target region while the source region still held a soft throttle; (2) circuit resets triggered by failover performed a non-idempotent KV eviction which could cause a tenant to be over-evicted and re-enter throttling sooner than intended.

This PR introduces a time-windowed tenant throttler that coordinates a short-lived leader token for per-tenant throttles across regions (windowed consensus) and a safe, idempotent reset token for KV/circuit resets. The goal is to make graceful degradation deterministic during failover windows and avoid double-application of throttles.

Design summary (high level):
- Add a lightweight reset_coordinator service that piggybacks on the existing region heartbeat stream; it issues a transient UTC-window token (window_id + expiry) for tenant throttles and resets.
- Throttler now accepts a window_token; when a region receives a handoff it consults local coordinator state to decide whether it should apply a new throttle or inherit an existing window token. Tokens are designed to be short-lived (default 6s) to limit cross-region staleness but long enough to cover KV handoff latency spikes.
- Circuit reset path changed to emit a reset_token (idempotent UUID tied to window_token). Applying a reset with the same reset_token is a no-op to prevent double-eviction.
- Fallback: if coordinator is unreachable, throttler falls back to deterministic tie-breaker (region-id hash) plus extended backoff to avoid immediate double-throttle while still allowing traffic.

What changed (summary of patches):
- src/serving/throttler.go: implement window-token acceptance, new decision path for applyThrottle().
- src/serving/consensus/reset_coordinator.go: new coordinator component (keeps in-memory window state, exposes minimal API).
- internal/kv/reset_idempotency.go: idempotent reset helper, persistent short-lived marker in local metadata store.
commits: a1d2f3c: add reset_coordinator skeleton and window token model
b4e5f6a: implement window-token logic in throttler and tests
c7d8e9f: add idempotent reset helper and integrate with KV eviction
d1e2f3b: e2e scenario for cross-region handoff and added dashboard panels
e4f5a6b: small lint/test fixes after review
ci_checks: bench - passed (p99 latency +1.3% in degenerate synthetic; documented)
review_conversation: Lena Morris (2026-02-26): Requested changes - please make window duration configurable and add a defend-against-time-drift test for coordinator. Also include a short note in the RFC about token expiry semantics.
Aisha Patel (2026-02-27): Addressed - added config flag 'tenant_throttle.window_seconds' with default 6s and added TestCoordinatorClockDrift in handler_test.go. Updated RFC. PTAL.

Diego Alvarez (2026-03-01): Comment - we should avoid doing a network call on the hot path. Confirmed coordinator lookup is in-memory with eventual async refresh; added a note and microbenchmark. Approved after that clarification.
Sophie Chen (2026-03-03): Approved - tests look comprehensive. Suggest watching tenant-throttle rate per-region for a deployment window.
rollout_plan: Step 1: canary deploy coordinator to staging region + run e2e scenario (automated). Step 2: enable windowed throttler in a single region with feature flag (rollout 10% tenants) for 2 hours and monitor dashboards (tenant-throttle.rate, p99 latency, failover_count). Step 3: full roll across regions. Rollback: disable feature flag which reverts to deterministic tie-breaker behavior.
monitoring_and_metrics: Added dashboard 'tenant-throttle' with panels: per-tenant throttle-rate, per-region window-token issuance, reset_token collision count, KV-eviction-rate, p99 latency for throttled vs non-throttled. Alert: increase in reset_token collisions > 1/min triggers pager. Watch list during rollout: throttle-rate spike, p99 latency changes, RecoveredFailoverCount.
qa_steps: 1) Run tests/e2e/regional_failover_throttle_test.go locally (requires multi-region test harness). 2) Simulate handoff with overlapping window by injecting artificial delay on source region and verify no double-throttle occurs. 3) Verify applying the same reset_token twice does not change KV metadata. 4) Canary with 10% tenants and verify dashboards for 1 hour.
known_issues:
- Benchmarked a small p99 latency regression (+1.3%) in synthetic high-concurrency degenerate cases; mitigations documented (tune window length, increase batching).
- If coordinator is partitioned for > window duration, system falls back to deterministic tie-breaker which can cause very short-lived soft double-throttle; this is acceptable per SLO but will be tracked via alerts.
